standard_prerequisites.name: Spans, cocones and the universal property of a pushout
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a span D = (A <-f- C -g-> B) and a type E, a cocone under D with vertex E is a triple (i,j,h) with i : A -> E, j : B -> E and h : Prd{c:C} i(f(c)) = j(g(c)); a pushout of D is a cocone that is initial, i.e. the induced map (D-pushout -> E) -> cocone(D,E) is an equivalence.
standard_prerequisites.use: The theorem is stated entirely in the language of cocones and pushouts, and the proof manipulates the two cocone types that appear in the square at source lines 994-1003.

standard_prerequisites.name: Truncation as a higher inductive type, its recursion and its naturality
standard_prerequisites.statement: For n >= -1 the n-truncation trunc n A is generated by tproj n : A -> trunc n A together with hub and spoke constructors; recursion into an n-type E is by a map on the points, and the naturality homotopies nat^f_n : trunc n f (tproj n a) = tproj n (f a) are the book's equation 7.3.4.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof uses that a map trunc n D -> E into an n-type E is the same as a map D -> E (source line 1005), and it invokes the naturality homotopies explicitly when defining the lowest horizontal arrow (source lines 1028-1034).

standard_prerequisites.name: Function extensionality and the two-out-of-three property for equivalences
standard_prerequisites.statement: happly is quasi-inverse to funext, so a homotopy between functions gives a path of functions and conversely; and in a commuting square of types, if two of the three maps are equivalences then so is the third.
standard_prerequisites.use: The middle horizontal arrow is an equivalence only because both lower vertical arrows are happly (source lines 1017-1023), and the argument applies two-out-of-three twice (source lines 1005-1006 and 1037).

core_obligations: Set up the commuting square of cocone types at source lines 994-1003 and observe that the upper horizontal arrow is an equivalence because E is an n-type while the right vertical arrow is an equivalence because c is a pushout cocone (source line 1005).

Prove that the upper square commutes by a three-step reassociation of the composite t o trunc n c o tproj, using the functoriality of the cocone action for the first step and the identity tproj n o c = trunc n c o tproj n for the second (source lines 1007-1016).
Show that the middle horizontal arrow is an equivalence by writing both lower vertical arrows as happly and citing function extensionality (source lines 1017-1023).

Define the lowest horizontal arrow explicitly on triples (i,j,p) with its coherence path q built from the naturality homotopies nat^f_n and nat^g_n (source lines 1024-1035), and note that it is induced by an equivalence of cospans (source line 1036).

Reduce the remaining goal, commutation of the lower square, to an equality of three component paths after applying happly, and discharge the first and third by happly being quasi-inverse to funext and the second by the general lemma relating happly to precomposition (source lines 1037-1061).

proof_roadmap.step: Build the square of cocone and function types and reduce, by two-out-of-three, to commutation of the upper square plus equivalence of the middle arrow.
Check the upper square by reassociating the truncated cocone, and the middle arrow by identifying both vertical maps with happly.
Construct the lowest horizontal arrow from an equivalence of cospans and reduce again by two-out-of-three to the lower square.
Verify the lower square componentwise through happly, using funext/happly invertibility and the happly-precomposition lemma.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 7.4.12 at source lines 984-989, with the author's complete 73-line proof at source lines 990-1062. The proof is not a formal consequence of the statement: it builds a two-by-two diagram of cocone types (source lines 994-1003), applies the two-out-of-three property for equivalences twice (lines 1005-1006 and 1037), and the middle horizontal arrow is an equivalence only because both lower vertical arrows are happly and hence equivalences by function extensionality (lines 1017-1023). The remaining content is the lower square: the coherence path q of the lowest arrow has to be assembled from the naturality homotopies nat^f_n and nat^g_n (lines 1027-1035), and the composite obtained that way must then be compared component by component through happly with the composite coming from transport along the cocone (lines 1042-1058). A statement that truncation preserves pushouts gives no hint that this alignment of transport, function extensionality and cocone functoriality is what has to be checked.
